lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

informal_arrangement.description: Whether the claimant is looking after someone else's child through an informal arrangement.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. 

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions. Let me start by gathering some information:

Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here in the UK. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know about Alex.

Before I can assess your eligibility, I need to read the official guidance on Child Benefit eligibility. Let me do that now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting. Now I have the official guidance, let me ask you a few questions to assess your eligibility for Alex.

You mentioned Alex lives with you in the UK. Are you responsible for Alex - meaning do you provide for his day-to-day needs such as food, clothes, and accommodation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am responsible for him. I look after Alex day-to-day - I provide his food, clothes, and he lives in my home. Though I should mention, I'm not actually his parent. I look after him through an informal arrangement with a friend.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful information.

To help me assess your situation properly, I need to ask: Is your local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance as part of this informal arrangement?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards his accommodation or maintenance. It's just an informal arrangement between me and his parent - I'm looking after him, but there's no council involvement or payments.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's very helpful.

Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else claimed it since he came to live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him, and no one else has made a claim for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just one final question to complete my assessment:

Do you have the right to reside in the UK? For example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, or another immigration status that gives you the right to reside here?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have the right to reside in the UK. I'm a UK citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- He lives with you in the UK
- You are responsible for his day-to-day care, providing his food, clothes, and accommodation
- The UK government rules specifically allow Child Benefit claims for informal arrangements where you're looking after a friend or relative's child
- The local council is not paying towards his care
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- You are a UK citizen with the right to reside in the UK

All the eligibility criteria are met for you to claim Child Benefit for Alex. You can proceed with making a claim.

**Please note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay a High Income Child Benefit tax charge, but you can still claim the benefit.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
